subject.title: fix(plugins): preserve state on npm metadata failures

question: Should this narrower, proof-positive PR be the canonical fix for the destructive plugin-state transition, or should the broader overlapping PR carry the release fix?
rationale: Both open PRs address the same P0 lifecycle defect, but the competing branch includes an additional update-check parser change; automation cannot choose which scope maintainers want to land and support.

options.title: Land this focused PR
options.body: Rebase and land this proven lifecycle fix, then close the overlapping PR or split out its independently needed update-check parser change.

options.title: Land the broader candidate
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106436 if its additional update-check parser change is required in the same release, and close this PR after that branch is viable and selected.

options.title: Retain fail-closed cleanup
options.body: Pause both candidates only if registry metadata failures are intentionally considered sufficient reason to disable an already-installed plugin despite the documented recovery impact.

recommendation.title: Land this focused PR
recommendation.body: Rebase and land this proven lifecycle fix, then close the overlapping PR or split out its independently needed update-check parser change.

likelyOwner.reason: The disableOnFailure lifecycle and its state-cleanup policy appear to originate in their work, making them the best available owner for selecting the intended failure behavior and canonical branch.
